title: Air Traffic Control Datalink Router — Removal from the Upper Avionics Rack
abstract: Removal of the air traffic control datalink router and its mounting tray from the upper avionics rack, with the coaxial handling precautions and the shelf position recording required before a relocation.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to remove the air traffic control datalink router and its mounting tray from the upper avionics rack, for replacement or for a shelf relocation.
sections.job_setup_note: Electrical power must be removed before the rack is opened. The coaxial connection to the antenna is torque sensitive and must be released with the correct tool; a bent centre pin is not repairable on the aircraft. The shelf position of both the router and the display interface unit must be recorded before removal, because on an unmodified aircraft they are not in the position the illustrated parts figure shows.
sections.procedure: 1. Remove electrical power from the aircraft and put the warning notice in position. 2. Open the upper avionics compartment access in zone 163. 3. Record the shelf position of the router and of the display interface unit. 4. Release the coaxial connection with the coaxial insertion tool. CAUTION: DO NOT PULL ON THE COAXIAL CABLE TO RELEASE THE CONNECTOR. THE CENTRE PIN BENDS AND THE CABLE MUST THEN BE REPLACED. 5. Fit the protective cap on the coaxial connector. 6. Release the rack retaining latch and pull the router forward until the rear connector separates. 7. Support the router with both hands and remove it from the rack. WARNING: THE ROUTER WEIGHS 9 KG AND IS REMOVED ABOVE SHOULDER HEIGHT. USE THE ACCESS PLATFORM AND A SECOND PERSON. 8. Put the router in an antistatic bag. 9. Remove the four tray retaining screws and remove the mounting tray. 10. Examine the shelf face and the rear connector for damage or discolouration and record the condition. 11. Install the protective cover on the open shelf position.
sections.close_out: Make sure that the coaxial connector is capped and supported and that no cable is left hanging on its connector. Close the compartment access if no further work is planned. Record the removed router part number, the shelf position it came from and the shelf face condition.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Step 3 is mandatory on aircraft pre MOD-146680 because the shelf positions differ from the illustrated parts figure.

safety_precautions: Remove electrical power from the aircraft.
Use the access platform; the rack is above shoulder height.
Put the warning notice in position.
